title: Catching Bugs
description: Learn how to use safety nets (try and except) to catch errors and prevent your game from crashing!

content.value: No matter how good a wizard you are, sometimes your spells go wrong. In coding, if a user inputs something bad, or if you try to divide a number by 0, the program crashes immediately! To prevent this, Python gives us a safety net: the `try` and `except` block.

We put code that might crash inside a `try` block. Below it, we write an `except` block. If the `try` code throws an error, instead of crashing, Python immediately jumps to the `except` block and runs the safety code!

Without `try`/`except`, your game or app would close immediately and show an ugly computer error screen to players. With it, you can print a friendly helper message and keep the application running smoothly!

practice.question: Wrap the division code below in a try/except block. If it succeeds, it should print the result. If it fails, print 'Division failed!'
practice.starterCode:
numerator = 10
denominator = 0

# Add try/except block to handle division safely
result = numerator / denominator
print(result)
